newsitem.title: USA: Unisource to sell unit to Bunzl.
newsitem.headline: Unisource to sell unit to Bunzl.

text.p: Unisource Worldwide Inc, a paper products and supply systems distributor, said Friday it has agreed to sell its Grocery Supply Systems unit and related U.S. operations to Bunzl Plc for about $88 million in cash.
Unisource said price is subject to changes based on valuations at the time of the deal's closing, expected to be by September 30, it said.

Ray Mundt, chairman and chief executive officer of Unisource, said that although the company is pleased with the top-line growth of its U.S. grocery supply business, those operations have not been profitable.
The sale, he said, is "in keeping with our mission of building value for shareholders over the long term."
"We expect to reinvest the proceeds in our successful supply systems businesses," he said.
Unisource's U.S. grocery supply systems business, which it started in 1993, currrently has more than $300 million in annual revenues.
Unisource also operates a successful grocery supply distribution business in Canada which is integrated with its supply systems operations there.
Grocery supply represents nearly a quarter of Unisource Canada's supply systems revenues, and Unisource is "fully committed to that business and intends to grow it aggressively."

Unisource, with annual revenues in excess of $7 billion, provides plastic films and containers, corrugated containers, packaging equipment and supplies and sanitary maintenance products to customers in the manufacturing, food processing, health care, hospitality and other industries.
Bunzl distributes, convertes and manufactures paper and plastic based products. Revenues in 1996 were 1.8 billion sterling.

Its unit, St. Louis, Mo.,-based Bunzl Distribution USA, distributes paper and plastic supplies to supermarkets, contract caterers, fast food suppliers and independent local distributors, represents more than forty percent of total corporate revenues.
